Built around a real moment

03 / PROJECT NOTES
01

One person, one task

Ana Martinez is a fictional community health nurse in a teaching-clinic scenario in Phoenix, Arizona. At the end of a screening session, she has limited time to review follow-ups. This prototype lets her explore how a model might flag records for review. It has not been tested at a clinic and must not be used to prioritize actual patients.

02

Public data. Reproducible model.

768 records from the public Pima Indians Diabetes dataset, originally attributed to NIDDK. The dataset describes women aged 21+ of Pima heritage. The target is the dataset’s binary diabetes label, not future onset.

Stratified 75/25 split, seed 42: 576 training and 192 test records. Zero glucose, blood pressure and BMI values become missing; median imputation and standardization are fitted only on training data. Logistic regression uses scikit-learn defaults with max_iter=1000.

Public dataset source ↗
03

Where it falls short

Four measurements cannot describe a person’s full health. Classes overlap; missing measurements and unmeasured clinical context can cause mistakes. The selected error above demonstrates this, but its cause cannot be proven from this dataset.

This historical, narrow dataset does not validate the model for men, children, other communities, or modern clinical workflows. No prospective, external or calibration validation has been done. Next: evaluate a locked threshold on another suitable public dataset before any clinical research.
